spec.full_target: For every prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer λ with 0 ≤ λ < p, and admissible lattice M in V(λ), M⊗_Z K is irreducible for L(K).
spec.conclusion: For every prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer λ with 0 ≤ λ < p, and admissible lattice M in V(λ), M⊗_Z K is irreducible for L(K).

propositions.statement: For every prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer λ with 0 ≤ λ < p, and admissible lattice M in V(λ), M⊗_Z K is irreducible for L(K).

argument.text: Fix arbitrary p,K,λ,M satisfying the target. Write R=Z_(p), choose the standard basis e_i=y^i v_+/i! (0≤i≤λ) of V(λ), and write X_r=x^r/r!, Y_r=y^r/r!. The sl2 relations and highest-weight equations give X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r), Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r), with out-of-range terms zero. Thus the operators are integral in this basis. Localize M to M_R=R⊗_Z M. Admissibility makes it stable under X_r,Y_r. The matrix-unit operators satisfy Y_λX_λ=E_λλ, X_(λ-i)E_λλ=E_iλ, and E_λλY_(λ-j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. Because λ<p, all binom(λ,j) are units of R, hence each E_ij=E_iλE_λj lies in the localized operator algebra and preserves M_R. Define J_i={c∈C:c e_i∈M_R}. Since E_ii projects M_R onto J_i e_i and M_R is finite over R, J_i is finite over R; it is nonzero since M_R spans V(λ) over C. E_ij and E_ji imply J_i=J_j; call this common module J. The projections sum to the identity, so M_R=⊕_{i=0}^λ J e_i. M_R is free of rank λ+1 over R, whence J is finite torsion-free of rank one. Explicitly, choose a nonzero a∈J; rank one means every element of J is a rational multiple of a. Finite generation gives a finite set of rational multipliers; taking their minimum p-adic valuation shows J=bR for some b∈C, so J is free rank one. (This also covers λ=0.) The isomorphism R→J identifies M_R with the standard module in the basis b e_i and intertwines x,y,h. Reduction modulo p identifies M_R/pM_R with the standard module over F_p, and extension of scalars identifies it with M⊗_Z K. Since r! is invertible modulo p for r≤λ, the divided powers X_r,Y_r on this module are scalar multiples of x^r,y^r. The matrix-unit identities therefore show that the algebra generated by x,y contains every E_ij, including when p=2. A submodule W is stable under these operators. If w=Σ c_i e_i∈W is nonzero, choose c_i≠0; then E_ji w=c_i e_j for every j, so W contains every basis vector and equals the module. The dimension λ+1 is positive. This proves irreducibility for every admissible lattice and all stated parameters.
